name: Emon Roy Bappy
headline: Research and Development Engineer
summary:
Currently, I am a Research and Development Engineer at Cybernetics Hi-Tech Solutions (Pvt.) Ltd. where I am focused on the development and analysis of military robots for Bangladesh Army. Our team has already delivered two Explosive Ordinance Disposal Remotely Operated Vehicles (EOD-ROVs), which have been deployed in United Nations Peacekeeping Missions. Currently, I am working on a Man-Portable EOD ROV project along with my teammates. My key responsibilities include Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DfMA), stress analysis, structural topology optimization, additive manufacturing methods for prototyping like Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM), molding of soft materials like silicone, subtractive manufacturing like CNC milling and Electro Discharge Machining (EDM). Recently, we have started working on composite materials. For the first time in Bangladesh’s history, we successfully implemented the resin infusion method to manufacture structural components using carbon fiber, achieving an industrial-grade solution within our own composite fabrication lab. This milestone not only demonstrates our manufacturing capabilities and knowledge but also creates a precedent for the country’s manufacturing infrastructure. 
 During my undergraduate studies in Mechanical Engineering at Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET), I built a strong foundation in electromechanical systems, computer-aided design, PCB design, and finite element analysis, which naturally pushed me to explore the intersection of robotics and manufacturing. As a third-year student in the mechanical department, I collaborated with my team to develop a bio-inspired soft robotic fish and a mechanical solution for variable capacity cooling tower. During my undergraduate thesis, I designed and fabricated a soft robotic actuator to replace the conventional rigid actuator in the medical robots used for Minimally Invasive Surgery (MIS). The soft actuator has three degrees of freedom to reach any area at the time of surgery, minimizing the number of incisions and reducing patient’s recovery time. 
 My goal is to pursue cutting-edge research that bridges the robotics field and manufacturing methods, ultimately contributing to the development of resilient and intelligent manufacturing solutions for humanitarian applications.

projects.longDescription:
Currently, we are developing a man-transportable EOD ROV, building on our experience with the previously developed medium-platform EOD ROV, Jontro Soinik v1.0. We began by analyzing the limitations of the earlier robot and identifying new challenges associated with designing a smaller platform. In the next phase, our focus was on constructing a lightweight structure that maximizes strength, maintains a low center of gravity, and introduces a new degree of freedom in the arm through a screw-based telescopic beam. To further reduce weight and enhance mechanical performance, we are integrating carbon fiber components into the robot. These parts are fabricated in-house using resin infusion, compression molding, and hand layup techniques within our composite fabrication laboratory.
The Man-Transportable EOD ROV is a compact bomb disposal robot built for high-stakes counter-IED operations. It navigates complex terrain with ease, using a dual-mode drive system and adaptive flipper mechanisms. The detachable manipulator arm offers precise control and tool-mounting flexibility, making it ideal for handling hazardous materials. Operators benefit from real-time situational awareness through a multi-camera setup, including a PTZ unit and wrist-mounted views. The robot’s control unit features a daylight-readable display and supports both wired and wireless communication for uninterrupted mission execution. Its rugged build and shock-absorbing design ensure durability in harsh environments. Integrated overload protection and intelligent motion control enhance operational safety and reliability. Designed for tactical deployment, the Man-Transportable EOD ROV combines mobility, modularity, and mission-ready resilience in a compact form.

projects.description: Jontro Soinik 1.0 (JS1.0) is Bangladesh’s third generation and most advanced indigenously developed Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) with environmental adaptability and disrupter firing capacity, which is first of its kind, engineered for ...
projects.longDescription:
Jontro Soinik 1.0 (JS1.0) is Bangladesh’s third generation and most advanced indigenously developed Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) with environmental adaptability and disrupter firing capacity, which is first of its kind, engineered for rapid deployment and rugged performance in high-risk environments. Successfully tested by the Bangladesh Army, including live disrupter firing and IP55 water protection trials, it proves its readiness for real-world missions. Equipped with advanced electronics like GPS, thermal imaging, IR night vision, 4x optical zoom, and a 2MP camera system, it supports precision surveillance and remote neutralization of threats. With robust mechanical capabilities—stair climbing, slope handling (up to 40°), 360° claw rotation, 40kg grip force, and a lifting capacity of up to 20kg—the ROV is built for maneuverability and strength. Its 16Ah battery enables extended operations with active/passive overload protection, self-diagnostics, and fast recharging. Designed for battlefield reliability, Jontro Soinik 1.0 embodies innovation, adaptability, and national pride in defense technology. 
 Jontro Soinik 1.0 is set for deployment in 2025 under the UN Peacekeeping Mission in the Republic of the Congo.

projects.longDescription: Smart Soinik 1.0 (SS1.0) is the second-generation, indigenously developed Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) from Bangladesh, designed for rapid deployment and unmatched performance in high-risk operational environments. Rigorously tested and validated by the Bangladesh Army, SS1.0 combines cutting-edge electronics — such as thermal imaging, IR night vision, 4× optical zoom, and high-resolution video capture — with rugged mechanical strength, including stair-climbing ability, 30° slope handling, 360° claw rotation, and a powerful 40 kg grip force. Powered by a 16 Ah battery system with overload protection, self-diagnostics, and fast recharge capability, it ensures extended field endurance and operational reliability. On May 5, 2024, Smart Soinik 1.0 was officially gifted to the Peruvian Armed Forces by the Bangladesh Army and is now proudly deployed under the United Nations Peacekeeping Mission in the Republic of Mali, showcasing Bangladesh's growing footprint in global defense innovation and humanitarian operations.

projects.title: Hilsha-Bot
projects.subtitle: A Bio-Inspired Soft Robotic Fish
projects.description: This bio-inspired soft robotic fish intended for concealment during tasks like underwater wildlife monitoring or reconnaissance. Its construction utilizes a soft silicone material covering a continuum structure, essential for replicating the natural, flexible undulatory ...
projects.longDescription: This bio-inspired soft robotic fish intended for concealment during tasks like underwater wildlife monitoring or reconnaissance. Its construction utilizes a soft silicone material covering a continuum structure, essential for replicating the natural, flexible undulatory movement of aquatic species. Propulsion is achieved using a soft tail actuator that executes a fish-like undulating motion, classified specifically as carangiform swimming. This natural method of locomotion is crucial because it allows the robot to integrate into the aquatic environment without disturbing other underwater entities. The tail movement is driven by a curved single-shaft mechanism which reciprocates the tail's sheets left and right to generate the required thrust. Depth control is managed by an innovative buoyancy control unit housed within the body. This unit operates through a piston-cylinder mechanism that creates a vacuum to adjust the overall specific weight of the robot. This vacuum piston-based approach offers the significant benefit of a longer operational period compared to traditional systems constrained by gas depletion. The robot is equipped with artificial pectoral and dorsal fins that collaboratively manage movement direction and stability. The pectoral fins control steering by generating lift forces, while the dorsal fin enhances overall stability, and an enclosure protects the sensitive electronics housed in the head section

projects.title: Soft Robotic Actuator
projects.subtitle: A Tendon-Driven Soft Actuator for Surgical Operation
projects.description: The soft actuator is a tendon-driven soft continuum robot designed for minimally invasive surgery. It is fabricated primarily from inert and biocompatible silicone rubber, utilizing a process that includes Fused Deposition Modelling for creating molds and subsequent liquid silicone rubber...
projects.longDescription: The soft actuator is a tendon-driven soft continuum robot designed for minimally invasive surgery. It is fabricated primarily from inert and biocompatible silicone rubber, utilizing a process that includes Fused Deposition Modelling for creating molds and subsequent liquid silicone rubber moulding. The actuator achieves a minimum of three degrees of freedom, including bending along two axes and rotation around its central axis. The structure is based on repeating single units, with a typical diameter of 15 mm. These units are assembled by routing tension cables, which can be made of material like unfilled Nylon 6.6, through their multiple circular channels. The system operates by applying tension to these cables to induce bending or rotation.The finalized design (Version 2.1) features separate units dedicated to bending and rotation functionalities, enhancing efficiency, and includes an additional internal hole to accommodate a tool grabbing mechanism and power cable routing. A thin rigid layer is used between adjacent units to help minimize frictional loss. Control is managed through a sophisticated closed-loop system incorporating four DC motors connected to the tendons, an Arduino development board, and a custom PCB, using motor current as real-time feedback. Finite element analysis was utilized during development to predict the structure’s deformation and stress behavior under load

projects.title: Titan, A Large Scale FDM Printer
projects.subtitle: A FDM 3D Printer with a Bed Volume of 510mm×510mm×550mm
projects.description: Titan is a large-format FDM printer designed for high-speed, precision additive manufacturing with a 510 × 510 × 550 mm build volume, ±0.1 mm accuracy, and 0.02 mm repeatability; it features CoreXY motion with GT2 belts, a direct-drive dual-gear extruder (MK8), a 0.8 mm swappable nozzle, and a heated...
projects.longDescription: Titan is a large-format FDM printer designed for high-speed, precision additive manufacturing with a 510 × 510 × 550 mm build volume, ±0.1 mm accuracy, and 0.02 mm repeatability; it features CoreXY motion with GT2 belts, a direct-drive dual-gear extruder (MK8), a 0.8 mm swappable nozzle, and a heated glass bed up to 120°C. The hotend reaches 300°C for engineering-grade thermoplastics, powered by a Bigtreetech controller with TMC2209 drivers running Marlin 2.0 firmware. Titan includes a 4.3 inch touchscreen with jog wheel, Wi-Fi, Ethernet, and USB-C connectivity. Safety features comprise thermal-runaway protection, power-loss resume, and door interlock. The MeanWell 24V / 30A PFC power supply ensures stable operation. Titan supports rapid prototyping and functional part fabrication with silent actuation and high-flow extrusion. Its optimized motion system enables smooth, vibration-free performance. The printer achieves up to 200 mm/s print speed, with a recommended range of 60–120 mm/s. Layer resolution spans 50–400 µm for fine detail and robust builds. Titan is ideal for research, industrial prototyping, and large-scale fabrication workflows.
